items.front: In IAM, an application on EC2 instances must call AWS APIs without a stored key. What do you use?
items.back: An IAM role through an instance profile.
items.extra: [AWS delivers the temporary credentials of an IAM role to that compute resource](../facts/iam.md#iam-compute-services-receive-role-credentials-no-keys-needed).

items.front: In IAM, SCP or permissions boundary: which one limits the root user of a member account?
items.back: The SCP.
items.extra: An SCP limits principals [including the member account's root user](../facts/iam.md#iam-scp-applies-to-member-root-user); you [cannot set a permissions boundary for the root user](../facts/iam.md#iam-root-user-no-identity-policies-or-boundary).

items.front: In IAM, can a bucket policy name an IAM group as its principal?
items.back: No. Name a role or a user instead.
items.extra: You [cannot identify a user group as a principal](../facts/iam.md#iam-principal-group-cannot-be-principal).

items.front: In IAM, trust policy or permissions policy: which one names who can assume the role?
items.back: The trust policy.
items.extra: The trust policy names [who can assume the role](../facts/iam.md#iam-role-trust-policy-names-who-can-assume), and the permissions policy decides what the session can do.

items.front: In AWS Organizations, can an SCP grant a permission to a role?
items.back: No. An SCP never grants permissions.
items.extra: To give access, [the administrator must still attach identity-based or resource-based policies](../facts/iam.md#iam-scp-never-grants-permissions).

items.front: In IAM, a third-party vendor needs access to your account, MOST secure. What do you use?
items.back: A cross-account role with an external ID condition.
items.extra: The external ID is [an sts:ExternalId condition in the role's trust policy](../facts/iam.md#iam-external-id-prevents-confused-deputy), and the vendor gives a value that is unique to you.

items.front: In IAM, same-account or cross-account request: which one needs an allow on both sides?
items.back: The cross-account request.
items.extra: Across accounts, AWS [allows the request only if both evaluations return Allow](../facts/iam.md#iam-eval-cross-account-needs-both-policies).

items.front: In IAM, can you revoke one leaked set of temporary security credentials?
items.back: No. Revoke the role's active sessions instead.
items.extra: One set [cannot be revoked](../facts/sts.md#sts-temporary-credentials-cannot-be-revoked-permissions-can-change). After you revoke the role's sessions, credentials [issued before the specified time become invalid](../facts/iam.md#iam-revoke-role-sessions-denies-credentials-issued-before).

items.front: In IAM, employees need one sign-in for many AWS accounts, managed centrally. What do you use?
items.back: IAM Identity Center.
items.extra: AWS calls IAM Identity Center its [recommended front door into AWS](../facts/iam.md#iam-idc-recommended-front-door-for-workforce).

items.front: In IAM, users of a mobile app must upload to Amazon S3 with temporary credentials. What do you use?
items.back: An Amazon Cognito identity pool.
items.extra: Cognito [identity pools deliver temporary IAM credentials](../facts/iam.md#iam-federation-cognito-identity-pools-deliver-iam-credentials) to the app users.

items.front: In IAM, servers on premises need AWS credentials without long-term keys. What do you use?
items.back: IAM Roles Anywhere.
items.extra: IAM Roles Anywhere [extends the capabilities of IAM to on-premises and hybrid cloud workloads](../facts/iam.md#iam-roles-anywhere-for-on-premises-and-hybrid-workloads) and [requires PKI, the ability to issue and manage certificates](../facts/iam.md#iam-roles-anywhere-for-on-premises-and-hybrid-workloads).

items.front: In IAM, limit a bucket to every account of your organization, with the LEAST operational overhead. Which condition key?
items.back: aws:PrincipalOrgID.
items.extra: Policies that use the key [automatically include the correct accounts](../facts/iam.md#iam-condition-key-principalorgid) when accounts join or leave.

items.front: In IAM, developers create roles, but the roles must never exceed a set maximum. What do you use?
items.back: A permissions boundary on the roles.
items.extra: A boundary sets the [maximum permissions that an identity-based policy can grant](../facts/iam.md#iam-permissions-boundary-sets-maximum-does-not-grant) to the role.

items.front: In IAM, can you set a permissions boundary for the root user?
items.back: No. In a member account, an SCP limits the root user.
items.extra: You [cannot set a permissions boundary for the root user](../facts/iam.md#iam-root-user-no-identity-policies-or-boundary).

items.front: In IAM, can one instance profile hold two roles?
items.back: No. One role per instance profile.
items.extra: An instance profile [can hold only one IAM role and this limit cannot be increased](../facts/iam.md#iam-instance-profile-one-role-and-metadata-credentials).

items.front: In IAM, service role or service-linked role: which one can an administrator edit?
items.back: The service role.
items.extra: For a service-linked role, an administrator [can view but not edit its permissions](../facts/iam.md#iam-service-linked-role-owned-by-service).

items.front: In AWS KMS, can an IAM policy alone allow use of a key whose key policy does not enable IAM policies?
items.back: No. The key policy must allow it.
items.extra: Without that key policy permission, [IAM policies cannot allow access to a KMS key](../facts/iam.md#iam-kms-iam-policy-needs-key-policy-permission). Chapter 06 covers key policies.

items.front: In IAM, you must find resources that allow public or cross-account access. What do you use?
items.back: IAM Access Analyzer.
items.extra: It [generates a finding for resources that allow public or cross-account access](../facts/iam.md#iam-access-analyzer-continuous-public-cross-account-findings).

items.front: In IAM, build a least-privilege policy from what a role really did. What do you use?
items.back: Access Analyzer policy generation from CloudTrail logs.
items.extra: Access Analyzer can [analyze your CloudTrail logs](../facts/iam.md#iam-access-analyzer-policy-generation-from-cloudtrail) and [generate an IAM policy based on that activity](../facts/iam.md#iam-access-analyzer-policy-generation-from-cloudtrail).

items.front: In IAM, does passing a role create a PassRole event in AWS CloudTrail?
items.back: No. PassRole is a permission, not an API call.
items.extra: Because [no CloudTrail logs are generated for IAM PassRole](../facts/iam.md#iam-passrole-is-a-permission-not-api-call), you review the call that created the resource.

items.front: In IAM, aws:SourceIp or aws:SourceVpce: which one matches requests through a VPC endpoint?
items.back: aws:SourceVpce.
items.extra: For aws:SourceIp, [when the request comes through a VPC endpoint the key is not available](../facts/iam.md#iam-condition-key-sourceip-public-only-not-via-vpce).

items.front: In IAM, can a user group contain another user group?
items.back: No. A group holds users, not groups.
items.extra: In IAM, [groups cannot be nested](../facts/iam.md#iam-groups-no-nesting-not-principals).

items.front: In IAM, does an expired console password stop the access keys of an IAM user?
items.back: No. The access keys keep working.
items.extra: The user loses console sign-in but [can continue to use their access keys](../facts/iam.md#iam-password-expired-user-keeps-access-keys).

items.front: In IAM, bucket policy or cross-account role: with which one does the caller keep its own permissions?
items.back: The bucket policy.
items.extra: With a resource-based policy, the caller [does not give up its permissions](../facts/iam.md#iam-cross-account-role-vs-resource-policy).

items.front: In IAM Identity Center, can Active Directory and an external SAML identity provider be connected at the same time?
items.back: No. One identity source at a time.
items.extra: IAM Identity Center connects [only one directory or one SAML 2.0 identity provider](../facts/iam.md#iam-idc-one-identity-source-at-a-time) at any given time.

items.front: In IAM, an AssumeRole session without DurationSeconds lasts {{c1::one hour}}.
In IAM, the shortest role session that AssumeRole accepts is {{c1::900 seconds (15 minutes)}}.
In IAM, the maximum session duration setting of a role can be {{c1::1 hour to 12 hours}}.
In IAM, role chaining limits a role session to a maximum of {{c1::one hour}}.
In IAM, one AWS account can have at most {{c1::5,000}} IAM users.
In IAM, the root user or one IAM user can register {{c1::up to eight MFA devices}}.
In IAM, one IAM user can have a maximum of {{c1::two access keys}}.
